title: Even If You Slit My Mouth
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Miroku, a yokai based on the slit-mouthed woman of Japanese urban legend, is fading because people no longer fear ghost stories. To survive she must enter an arranged engagement with Koichi Sano, heir of a family that looks after supernatural beings. They strike a deal: if she can frighten him before his eighteenth birthday the engagement is off, but if she falls for him she must marry him.
life_message: It holds up love that grows through patience and understanding, even between a monster and a human.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Miroku's pride as a feared legend drives her, though conflicts stay gentle.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The engagement is imposed, but the scare-or-love deal leaves room for choice.

Civic vs kin.evidence: The Sano clan's inherited role and family obligations frame the romance.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Koichi is clan head; Miroku sees him as lowly, a contest of status.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folklore, clan custom and arranged marriage guide life.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Miroku's survival is at stake, but the story turns toward feelings.

folkways.japan: The Kuchisake-onna urban legend, yokai belief and family-arranged marriage within an old household reflect Japanese folklore and ie (household) traditions.

winners_losers: Miroku and Koichi, if they choose each other, win; fear and indifference to old stories lose. Sympathy goes to the misunderstood spirit.
